nodes.content: Learn reduced models of partially observed Kuramoto–Sivashinsky dynamics preserving stationary energy distributions and responses to unseen forcing.
requirements: Stationary energy-distribution Wasserstein-1 error stays below 5% of the full-system distribution’s standard deviation.
Predict nonzero mean-energy responses to unseen weak forcing within 10% relative error against full-system simulations.

nodes.content: Train a control-affine latent SDE with fixed Fourier forcing injection, matching sparse KS observations, energy Wasserstein-1, and probe responses.
Can sparse-sensor training with mode-1 probes identify mean-energy responses to unseen weak mode-2 forcing?
Unforced trajectory fitting plus mode-1 probe matching identifies cross-mode coupling, yielding <10% mean-energy response error under unseen weak mode-2 forcing.
Train the latent SDE on unforced eight-sensor trajectories and mode-1 probes; benchmark mode-2 ±0.01 mean-energy responses against full KS.
On eight-sensor KS, stationary-energy W1 was 3.7% of full-system SD; mode-2 ±0.01 mean-energy response errors peaked at 7.6%.
Ablate mode-1 probe matching across five training seeds, comparing unseen mode-2 ±0.01 mean-energy response errors against full KS.
Across five seeds, mode-1 probe matching produced >10% mode-2 response error in three seeds, peaking at 24%.
Constraining unforced mode-1/mode-2 lagged covariances alongside mode-1 probes stabilizes cross-mode coupling, keeping unseen mode-2 response error <10% across five seeds.
Retrain five seeds with 0.5-time-unit mode-1/mode-2 lag-covariance loss; compare stationary-energy W1 and unseen mode-2 ±0.01 response errors against probe-only models.
Across five seeds, lag-covariance models achieved stationary-energy W1 of 3.2–4.6% of full-system SD and maximum mode-2 response error of 8.4%.
Validate five lag-covariance seeds under unseen phase-shifted mode-2 forcing at ±0.005, comparing mean-energy responses against 50 full-KS trajectories.
Against full KS, phase-shifted mode-2 ±0.005 responses exceeded 10% relative error in three of five seeds, peaking at 18%.
Phase-shift failures suggest missing mode-2 quadrature coupling; translation-equivariant dynamics with sine–cosine lag matching yield <10% ±0.005 response errors across seeds.
Implement equivariant drift and sine–cosine lag matching; benchmark five seeds on unseen mode-2 phases and energy W1 against KS.
Retrain five equivariant-drift seeds with quadrature matching; require W1≤4.6%-SD and <10% response error on previously failing ±0.005 phase-shifts.
Across five equivariant seeds, stationary-energy W1 was 3.1–4.3% of full-KS SD; phase-shifted mode-2 ±0.005 response errors peaked at 8.1%.
KS-Equivariance-v1 contains five trained latent-SDE checkpoints, quadrature-matching code, and reproducible energy-W1 and phase-shifted forcing benchmarks.
Adopt equivariant quadrature matching: it retains sub-5%-SD energy W1 and resolves phase-shift failures persisting after lag-covariance matching.
Fit a delay-coordinate NARMAX surrogate with state-dependent noise, energy-quantile calibration, and explicit Fourier-force projection onto eight sensors.
Does state-dependent NARMAX noise preserve stationary energy tails while delay-memory terms transfer weak forcing responses from eight sensors?
Four-lag NARMAX with energy-conditioned noise achieves energy Q95 error <8%, W1 <5%-SD, and unseen mode-2 mean-energy response error <10%.
Train five four-lag NARMAX seeds; benchmark energy Q95, W1, and mode-2 ±0.005 phase-shift responses against full KS and KS-Equivariance-v1.
Five NARMAX seeds achieved energy-Q95 errors ≤7.2%, W1 ≤4.7% of full-KS SD, and phase-shifted mode-2 ±0.005 response errors ≤9.3%.
Retain four-lag NARMAX as a viable alternative: all five seeds meet energy-W1 and unseen forcing-response targets.
Estimate a stochastic Koopman generator on eight-sensor delays, constraining its invariant energy law and Fourier-mode linear-response resolvent.
Fit eight-sensor delay-Koopman generators; calibrate invariant energy and mode-1 resolvents; test stationary W1 and unseen mode-2 responses.
Using KS-Equivariance-v1 benchmarks, fit five energy-calibrated delay-Koopman generators with mode-1 resolvents; compare energy W1 and unseen mode-2 responses.
KS-Koopman-v1 packages five calibrated generator fits, eight-sensor delay features, and evaluation scripts using KS-Equivariance-v1 forcing benchmarks.
Five Koopman fits achieved energy W1 of 3.5–4.8% of full-KS SD and unseen phase-shifted mode-2 response errors of 6.9–9.7%.
Stress-test KS-Koopman-v1 across five fits on unseen phase-shifted mode-3 ±0.005 forcing, comparing mean-energy responses with full KS.
For unseen phase-shifted mode-3 ±0.005 forcing, four of five Koopman fits exceeded 10% mean-energy response error; maximum reached 21%.
Defer Koopman as a general surrogate: mode-2 benchmarks pass, but four of five fits fail unseen mode-3 responses.
Learn a Mori–Zwanzig closure for three Fourier-mode pairs reconstructed from eight sensors, with causal memory and explicit forcing projection.
Can causal memory recover unseen phase-shifted mode-3 mean-energy responses from eight sensors without distorting stationary energy?
A causal six-time-unit memory kernel yields <10% unseen phase-shifted mode-3 response error and energy W1 <5%-SD across five seeds.
Using Koopman mode-2 and failed mode-3 benchmarks, test five six-unit-memory closures on phase-shifted mode-3 responses and stationary-energy W1.
Six-unit-memory closures achieved W1≤4.8% of full-KS SD; three of five exceeded 10% phase-shifted mode-3 response error (maximum 17%).
A translation-equivariant cross-mode memory kernel yields <10% phase-shifted mode-3 response error across five seeds while preserving energy W1 <5%-SD.
Train five translation-equivariant cross-mode memory closures; benchmark stationary-energy W1 and unseen phase-shifted mode-3 ±0.005 responses against full KS.
Five equivariant-memory seeds achieved energy W1 of 3.0–4.4% of full-KS SD and phase-shifted mode-3 response errors of 5.8–8.9%.
Test equivariant-memory closures at held-out mode-3 phases and ±0.0025 forcing, measuring mean-energy response error and stationary-energy W1.
Extend and validate KS-Koopman-v1 benchmarks with e10’s five closures, measuring stationary-energy W1 and held-out mode-3 ±0.0025 response errors.
KS-Koopman-v2 replaces Koopman-only scripts with matched energy-W1 and held-out mode-3 ±0.0025 benchmarks plus five equivariant-memory checkpoints.
At held-out mode-3 phases and ±0.0025 forcing, all five equivariant-memory closures kept energy W1≤4.4%-SD and mean-energy response errors≤9.2%.
Adopt equivariant-memory closure over plain memory: five seeds pass energy and mode-3 response targets, including held-out weaker forcing.
Train a diffusion transition model on eight-sensor histories with energy-quantile calibration and explicit Fourier-force conditioning.
Train five diffusion seeds on unforced and mode-1 data; evaluate stationary-energy W1 and held-out mode-2/3 responses against full KS.
Train five diffusion seeds; compare energy W1 and unseen mode-2/3 responses with KS-Koopman-v2, emphasizing Koopman’s failed mode-3 cases.
Five diffusion seeds achieved energy W1 of 3.6–4.9% of full-KS SD and unseen mode-2/3 response errors of 6.5–9.8%.
KS-Diffusion-v1 contains five force-conditioned transition checkpoints, energy-quantile calibration code, and matched KS-Koopman-v2 mode-2/3 benchmarks.
Retain diffusion as a viable comparator, not preferred: its margins trail latent-SDE, NARMAX, and memory closures; Koopman fails mode-3.
